mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior 5-quarter average coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity payoffs.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-quarter moving average
failure_condition: Over 30 instances where FEDFUNDS crosses above 5-QMA with no negative 20d SPX returns, or Rank IC > 0.05 in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in hourly wage growth (indirect via HOUST) signals labor market weakness that precedes S&P 500 declines over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% from the prior month while HOUST decreases by >2% from the prior month
failure_condition: In 5 consecutive such labor weakness events, the 60-day SPX forward return is positive or the interaction effect rank is above 0.1 in out-of-sample testing.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in retail sales (GDPC1) persists for three consecutive months and predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as investor confidence in consumption recovers.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth > 2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: Three such consumption recoveries occur but produce no statistically significant positive 20d SPX returns (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% from the prior month coincides with a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates soft demand.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% from prior month
failure_condition: Multiple INDPRO contractions >5% fail to precede negative 5-day SPX returns in out-of-sample walk-forward tests.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4% (UNRATE) while the Fed funds rate remains unchanged for two consecutive months, a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return is expected as a disinflation surprise.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% and FEDFUNDS unchanged for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Such dual signals occur but produce no statistically significant positive 20d SPX returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-week decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 0.2% followed by a rebound above 0.2% signals a cooling inflationary bias that precedes a positive 20-day SPX forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 0.2% for two consecutive weeks then crosses above 0.2% in the third week
failure_condition: Three such CPI cycles produce no positive 20d SPX returns (p > 0.05).
